acceptance.result: Bugfix, system-change, and product-change are mutually distinguished by behavior and governance surface; WFG-008 covers bounded system behavior, a small permission/business-rule change, and confirmed behavior restoration without prose-string tests.
System-change metadata uses schema: spec-driven, and source plus installed-target tests confirm no copied openspec/schemas/spec-driven directory.
OpenSpec 1.5.0 validates its built-in spec-driven Schema and the installed-target scenario exercises native proposal, specs, design, tasks, and apply/close dependencies.
Schema-aware implementation authorization governance applies to spec-driven after its complete planning dependency closure.
Spec-driven uses the non-product closeout contract with stable delta Requirement IDs, passed project-local evidence, and all four gate decisions, without product trace fields.
A clean installed target formally closes a spec-driven change, updates canonical specs, archives the change, and records schema spec-driven in generated history.
Change history, closeout diagnostics, Schema validation, generated navigation, and installer/runtime tests recognize spec-driven as supported.
Global BR/PRD proposal rules are product-change-only, while stable IDs, authorization, tasks, evidence, and formal close remain common governance.
